spec_match.rationale: On Chromium 157 the button runs the real default Element.setHTML(): script, onerror/onclick and javascript: hrefs (including the leading-space variant) are removed and svg/math survive script-free, which is the core contract, but setHTMLUnsafe and Document.parseHTML are never contrasted and the 'what the default blocks' list is static prose.

interactive.rationale: Three presets plus an editable textarea feed a real setHTML call whose rendered output and serialised HTML update on click.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb matches the flow, but the strip log appends a hard-coded 'Safe elements preserved (b, p, strong, em, a[href]...)' line whatever the input actually contained.

edge_cases.rationale: The tricky preset covers SVG-nested script, leading-space javascript:, comments and MathML, but empty input returns early and leaves the previous output on screen (verified), and nothing shows mXSS/namespace or style/data-attribute handling.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus.com/feature/5814067399491584 and MDN; the only spec link (feature index / policy-comparator) is https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/, whose abstract now says the draft 'should be no longer consulted' because the API moved into WHATWG HTML.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite runs 7/7 PASS on Chromium 157, but five assertions are existence checks and only one (setHTML strips <script>) is behavioural; nothing asserts on* handler removal, javascript: URL removal, that setHTML stays safe even with a permissive custom config, that a malformed SanitizerConfig throws TypeError, or what Document.parseHTML returns.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Every preset + Sanitize and the empty-input path were exercised at both viewports with 0 console errors and 0 failed requests, but the strip log rendered '✗ stripped:' with a blank label (see open questions). chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b); evidence is Playwright headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch.

telemetry_health.rationale: The shared /public/demo-telemetry.js is injected (runtime/resource errors would be captured) but the page emits no page-specific assertion or interaction events, and /telemetry/demo/events (Basic auth) was not queried in this pass.

design_system.rationale: Colours come from CSS variables, but badges use opacity:0.85 white-on-accent (contrast unverified) and several layout styles are inline.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons; the textarea is named only by aria-label (its visible 'Input HTML' caption is not a <label>), output/serialised/strip-log regions are not live regions, and the XSS preset string contains an injected role=button tabindex=0 onkeydown attribute set that looks like an automated a11y fixer mutated the payload. Accessibility tree not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level horizontal overflow at 360x740 (code blocks scroll internally) and the grid stacks, but 4 of 5 controls are under 44px tall on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Escape the strip-log labels; they inject live markup
openQuestions.detail: Labels '<script>', '<iframe>' and '<embed>/<object>' are interpolated into stripLog.innerHTML unescaped, so the log shows '✗ stripped:' with an empty label and creates real (empty) script/iframe/embed elements in the page. Verified on Chromium 157 with the XSS and tricky presets. A sanitizer demo must not have an innerHTML sink: build the log with textContent.

openQuestions.title: Remove the regex-plus-innerHTML 'fallback'
openQuestions.detail: Without setHTML the page regex-strips the input and writes it to innerHTML. Payloads such as <svg/onload=...> pass the regex, and the fallback teaches the exact anti-pattern the feature replaces. In unsupported browsers show the input as escaped text with an honest 'not supported' state instead of producing fake sanitised output.

openQuestions.title: Clear stale output on empty input and derive the 'kept' line from the real result
openQuestions.detail: Sanitising an empty textarea leaves the previous result on screen. The 'Safe elements preserved' line is hard-coded. Derive both from the actual sanitised DOM.

openQuestions.title: Add a setHTML vs setHTMLUnsafe vs parseHTML concept
openQuestions.detail: The spec's core safety guarantee is that setHTML/parseHTML always apply removeUnsafe, even with a permissive config, while setHTMLUnsafe/parseHTMLUnsafe honour it. Verified on Chromium 157: setHTML with elements:['script'] still drops the script, and setHTMLUnsafe with the same config keeps it. No concept shows this side by side.

openQuestions.title: Point the spec reference at WHATWG HTML, not the retired WICG draft
openQuestions.detail: wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api now states the draft 'should be no longer consulted' and that the API was merged into WHATWG HTML. Link the HTML Standard section (Sanitizer, SanitizerConfig, setHTML/parseHTML) from this concept and the feature index.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.query: sanitize untrusted HTML with setHTML instead of innerHTML
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use Element.setHTML()/Document.parseHTML(); a custom Sanitizer can only restrict, never re-allow XSS-unsafe markup; elements not in `elements` are removed with their content (use replaceWithChildrenElements to keep text); move parsed nodes rather than re-serialising through innerHTML.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Used as the grading reference for this critique (review only, no page edits). The page's fallback paths and its unescaped innerHTML log/readout writes run against this guidance; recorded as open questions.

guidanceConsulted.query: sanitize untrusted HTML with setHTML instead of innerHTML
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never write untrusted strings into innerHTML sinks; use textContent/DOM construction or a sanitizer/Trusted Types policy.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: user-supplied strings reach innerHTML in this page; recorded as a major open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region announcing dynamic log output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamically changing status/log output through an appropriate live region or <output>, keep native semantics and associated labels for controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: the page's changing readouts carry no aria-live/role=status; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: minimum touch target size for buttons on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep touch targets usable (~44px) and content within its space on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: measured controls below 44px tall at 360x740; recorded under mobile_desktop_parity.

summary: A working default-setHTML playground: the real API strips the expected vectors on Chromium 157 with a clean console. Its own strip log is an unescaped innerHTML sink that blanks the labels and injects elements. The unsupported-browser path is a regex-plus-innerHTML fake sanitizer. Browser evidence is Playwright, not chrome-devtools-mcp.
